# Committed cell identity registry review

Read-only audit of `OwnerStateWorld.#committedCellsByIdentity`. No source or tests were changed, and no tests, browser, benchmark, or server were run.

## Finding

The registry does not appear to protect an invariant that the committed capability cannot provide. `CommittedCellCapability` already carries the World secret, owner, site and cell in private fields; `resolve` checks all four, and `revoke` nulls both the secret and cell ([capability](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:110)). `OwnerStateWorld.#resolveCellIdentity` already exposes that exact check for cell handles ([resolver](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1772)). The registry’s `CommittedCellIdentity` value duplicates owner/site/cell, and its `handle` field has no reader ([type and map](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:375), [field](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:501)). Its only reads are `scalarSourceForChange` and `versionForChange` ([source lookup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1817), [version lookup](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1839)). Both already fall back to the public owner/site lookup when the identity is absent, foreign or misaddressed.

Each committed cell identity is created lazily at its first changed dispatch in `#dispatchState`; the registry then allocates one `{ owner, site, cell, handle }` record for that capability ([creation](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:2092)). This means removal saves the per-World WeakMap, the first-dirty per-cell registry record, its unused handle reference and the destroy-time delete. It does not remove capability or handle allocations, and it has no expected warm-write benefit: later writes reuse the capability and don’t allocate another registry entry.

## Lifecycle and fallback parity

- **Existing-cell publication:** candidate publication updates the committed cell in place and keeps its identity; new candidate cells start with no committed identity and receive one only after a committed dispatch ([publish](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1421), [candidate cell](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:964)). Capability resolution therefore continues to reach the current cell after publication without a registry entry.
- **Destroy/replacement:** `destroyOwner` revokes every cell capability before removing owner/cell payload, clears the cell’s identity/handle, then drops the payload ([destroy](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1983)). `resolveOwner` assigns increasing owner IDs; a replacement owner does not inherit the destroyed capability. Lane row reuse is separately guarded by generation. Direct capability resolution returns `null` after revocation, so stale changes still take owner/site fallback; the existing dead-owner assertion then throws as before.
- **Promotion and reentrant writes:** both mutate the same cell rather than replacing its identity. `scalarSourceForChange` must read the cell’s current value/source, not a captured source; `versionForChange` must return the cell’s current version. The capability points to that same cell and preserves this behavior. Newer writes remain protected by version checks in `clearChangesThrough` ([acknowledgement](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_state_world.ts:1883)).
- **Cross-World, forged, malformed and Proxy identities:** the private World secret and private-brand check reject a foreign capability, plain object, forged shape or Proxy wrapper. Owner/site mismatch also rejects an otherwise authentic capability. Preserve the existing owner/site fallback after any rejection. A `WeakMap.get` itself does not invoke traps on the identity object; the private brand check likewise should not inspect user properties. Do not replace capability validation with duck typing or direct property reads.
- **Dead-owner behavior:** after `destroyOwner`, `scalarSourceForChange` and `versionForChange` must still reach the same `#assertOwner` error through owner/site fallback. A revoked capability must not become a successful lookup, and a newly created owner at the same lexical site must not satisfy a stale identity.

## Observable accessor/reentry caveat

`StateChange` is an exported structural type and the two resolution methods accept an object with potentially accessor-backed fields at runtime. The current registry path checks identity first; a foreign/malformed identity reaches owner/site fallback without an extra owner/site read. An authentic same-World identity reads owner/site for registry address comparison and reads them again through `#assertOwner`/fallback as applicable. Replacing the map with a direct `resolve(identity, secret, change.owner, change.site)` call would evaluate owner/site getters before the resolver knows whether the identity belongs to this World. A getter may throw, count reads, or reenter/destroy the owner, so that changes observable behavior for exotic `StateChange` objects even though World-generated changes are plain records.

To remove the registry while preserving this ordering, first add a no-allocation private capability check that answers only “is this capability from this World?” without reading `change.owner` or `change.site`; only for an owned capability should the method read the address and call the existing exact `#resolveCellIdentity`. Keep owner/site fallback for all other cases. Preserve the current repeated reads if exact accessor behavior is a compatibility requirement; otherwise explicitly document and test any decision to snapshot fields once. This should remain an internal capability operation, not a new public identity API or a second registry.

## Finite parity tests before implementation

1. Extend `state_change_resolution_test.ts`: own identity resolves the same canonical source and current version before/after existing-cell publish; new candidate identity appears only on first committed dispatch; numeric → nonnumeric → numeric promotion continues to resolve the current source; repeated writes retain identity and `versionForChange` returns the newest version.
2. Preserve fallback cases: absent identity, foreign World identity, misaddressed own identity, arbitrary object identity, Proxy around an identity, and non-object malformed identity all resolve by owner/site exactly as before. Test both source and version methods.
3. Preserve revocation and payload lifetime: retained StateChange/handle after owner destruction cannot resolve; source/version methods throw for the dead owner; a replacement owner at the same component site cannot resolve the old identity. Include a retained capability while destroying a subtree so the old cell payload can be collected/released independently of the retained handle.
4. Test hostile `StateChange` accessors: owner/site getters that count reads, throw, or synchronously destroy the owner; a `cellIdentity` getter that returns different identities across reads. Assert the intended read order and exception/reentry outcome. Cover both source and version APIs. This is necessary because the map currently screens foreign identities before address getters.
5. Keep dirty acknowledgement coverage: call `clearChangesThrough` with an authentic stale change after a newer reentrant write and verify the newer version remains pending; call it with foreign/misaddressed identity and verify the owner/site fallback retains current semantics.

Relevant existing coverage is in [state_change_resolution_test.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/state_change_resolution_test.ts:23), [owner_prepared_identity_test.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/owner_prepared_identity_test.ts:15), and [state_change_identity_test.ts](/Users/tjw/Documents/Codex/2026-10-09/le/outputs/react-runtime-research/src/state_change_identity_test.ts:178). They cover publication, foreign/misaddressed fallback, dead-owner failure, promotion, stale capability, owner destruction, row reuse and reentrant acknowledgement, but not accessor evaluation order or Proxy state-change records.

## Recommendation

The registry is removable as a storage authority: the revocable capability already has the needed secret, address and cell identity, and its revoke operation severs payload retention even when callers retain stale handles. A safe patch should remove `CommittedCellIdentity`, the WeakMap, its set/delete, and the `handle` entry in the old registry value; route identity-bearing changes through capability authorization plus the existing fallback. Resolve the accessor-order caveat before editing. Report the cold allocation removed only; make no warm-path or general performance claim.
